business_problem: Bristol Myers Squibb needed to shorten expensive, operationally complex Phase III clinical trials and give research teams faster, clearer visibility into trial performance so they could react to issues earlier and bring therapies to patients more quickly.
solution_summary: Bristol Myers Squibb and Accenture built Workbench as a clinical-trial accelerator that combines generative AI, automation, and real-time operational data for drug-development teams. The broader partnership implemented more than 30 generative AI solutions across R&D, product development and supply, and commercialization, but Workbench became a focal system for trial operations. It gathers structured and unstructured trial data, organizes it into decision-ready views, and presents actionable insights to project teams. A recommendation feature tailors guidance by user role, study type, and trial context, while analysis of current and historical data helps anticipate emerging issues and propose interventions before delays grow. By integrating insights across transactional systems into one trusted operating layer, Workbench shifts trial execution from reactive coordination to proactive management and standardizes best practices across priority clinical programs.

data_flow: Structured and unstructured clinical-trial data is gathered into Workbench, where automation and generative AI organize it into decision-ready views. The recommendation feature analyzes current and historical signals by user role, study type, and trial context, then returns actionable guidance and issue-prevention insights to project teams through the Workbench interface.
business_outcome: Bristol Myers Squibb accelerated priority clinical trials, expanded use of a common trial-operations platform, improved visibility into key execution risks, and gave teams a faster way to learn from past studies and act before operational problems delay development.
